instructions: Assess only the listed primary candidates in a fresh invocation. Read their dialogue first, then the exact card; use the alternate only to judge meaningful differentiation. Supply six criterion ratings with specific turn evidence and full coach-2.0 findings. Do not invent missing backstory or assume earlier approval. No writer scores or rationales are supplied. Report real reservations and failures. Totals are calculated in code.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

card.title: Move It for Me
card.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut so we can have lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've been friends since school. Couldn't I have its place just once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds if I change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Put lunch in that exact slot, in pen. You've used pencil for me since school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you leave quiz night for your sister's first exhibition opening?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm captain. They'll think I've abandoned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them your sister needs you. I'd like that to outrank geography.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave after round one and say I've got a headache.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come after round one, but tell them it's for me. I want to rank above geography, not below a headache.

card.title: Hand It Over
card.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've spent hours on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

card.title: Put It Back Quietly
card.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plate's back in the cupboard, ready for Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take that one. The potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it under potatoes. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more before lunch. Keep the plain ones for spares; there's no need to count those today.

card.title: Talk Around the Mess
card.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum's coming for lunch. Is this spoon clean enough for her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spoon's fine. You haven't cleaned the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She checks cutlery. Could you check the forks while I finish this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've told her to bring rubber gloves and help you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a guest towel. Can you help me choose one without a faded stripe?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which label colour suits these boxes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't packed them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good labels prevent moving-day confusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'd better choose a colour the driver likes.

card.title: Spare Them the Hassle
card.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit down, love. You've been on the ward all night. I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's there a bucket by my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just catching a drip. Take the sofa; I've made you a tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay here. I'll bring your duvet down; upstairs needs a little drying before I put your bed back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enjoy your afternoon off. Your bike will be ready for tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's the repair shop asking me to collect a wheel?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've got your number on the ticket. I'll collect everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A wheel? Is the rest at another shop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only until four. Stay with your book; I've planned a route that gets all of it home before you need it.

card.title: Who Changed It?
card.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?
